checks: Opening a record follows its exact placement and shows its filing path without changing the typed identity
Settings opens as a retained Room beside an edited Preview without a Save/Pin prompt or consuming one of five pins
Explicit Settings navigation clears an excluding filter, expands the destination path and leaves unrelated folds intact
A matching Settings filter is retained and the existing Apply route still updates the original owner profile
Focusing retained Cabinet and Settings tabs follows the correct tree while preserving both drafts and the original Settings revision
The Cabinet word returns to the retained record room instead of leaving the Settings editor active
Show in cabinet reveals a filtered placement without reopening its form or overwriting writing
A second-project reference keeps its exact placement, canonical identity and original project instead of jumping to the owning home
An unavailable placement clears a misleading highlight and reports the bounded-view limit without substituting another record
Navigation retains the original memory revision guard; a later legacy edit still refuses stale Apply and preserves writing
Hatch, Work, Arrange, Rules and the checked record-action menu render as actual Qt popups without triggering their commands
Explore carries the checked reference placement into the left cabinet without changing the record or replacing the source Preview
Method inspection opens the original Atlas and preserves the edited source Preview
Operations and Context retain the cabinet identity and show real pending Agenda metadata without a job submission
The existing return-copy route retains the cabinet draft and source recovery while navigation leaves the source file unchanged
Resizing the left column keeps its expanded selected row in view without reopening the record or expanding a deliberately folded branch
The compact desktop retains the filing control, unfinished project writing and fixed Trash, Stop, monitors and return footer
Original source bytes/mode, imported reference, idea ownership, five-pin policy and Hatch commands survive all transitions
Repeated menu rebuild preserves original menu objects, QAction identities and keyboard shortcuts
Clean close removes the desktop lease; guarded provider, job submission and OS-priority routes were never called
